row.title: Normalization of a reduced curve is finite
row.statement: Let k be a field and let C be a reduced k-scheme of finite type, of pure dimension one (for example a reduced projective plane curve or an open subscheme of one). Then there exists a finite morphism nu:C~->C with the following properties: (1) C~ is regular of dimension one (equivalently normal: all local rings are DVRs or fields); (2) nu is an isomorphism over the regular locus of C and is birational on each irreducible component; (3) on an affine chart Spec A of C, nu is the morphism corresponding to the integral closure of A in its total ring of fractions; (4) nu is unique up to a unique C-isomorphism, and nu_*O_{C~} is a coherent O_C-module. No separability or perfectness hypothesis on k is needed.
row.strategy: Construct integral-component normalizations from module-finite affine integral closures and principal localizations on arbitrary overlaps, with identities inside each component function field; no separatedness assumption. Take their finite disjoint union. Identify Q(A) with the product of component fraction fields using minimal-prime separators g_i and summed denominators, then prove the finite product of integral closures is precisely the closure in Q(A). Integral dimension preservation and normal one-dimensional local rings give regularity. Localization and a finite quotient-module argument give the regular-locus isomorphism. Finite affine direct images give coherence, and canonical integral-closure algebras give the unique C-isomorphism.
